settings.title: Pointe Shoe Guide
settings.text:
Since our founder Jacob Bloch made his first pointe shoe in 1932, Bloch has been the innovation leader for these shoes, which epitomise the art of ballet. You’ll find our pointe shoes on the feet of leading professionals in dance companies around the world, as well as thousands of training ballet students.

Our handmade satin ballet pointe shoes balance superior construction with a dancer’s comfort. A correctly fitted Bloch pointe shoe considers all aspects of the shoe’s anatomy to ensure correct foot positions and the perfect leg line.

We strongly recommend that dancers visit one of our Bloch Stores for a professional fitting from one of our highly trained staff.

settings.title: Anatomy of a Pointe Shoe
settings.text:
1 – Throat Line
2 – Block/Box
3 – Modified Vamp
4 – Shank/Insole*
5 – Sock
6 – Drawstring
7 – Binding
8 – Vamp
9 – Platform
10 – Wing
11 – Side Seam
12 – Pleats
13 – Outsole
14 – Heel Strap


* Concealed inside under the sock

settings.title: Glossary of Terms
settings.text: Brush up on your pointe shoe terminology

settings.title: Binding
settings.text: The tape that finishes the top edge of the upper which also encases the drawstring.

settings.title: Block/Box
settings.text: The hardened surface area of a pointe shoe which includes the vamp, wings and platform, surrounds the front section of the foot. TheBlock/Boxis made from the application of numerous layers of special fabrics, all with different shapes, bound together by the paste in between each layer. This process is very similar to the process of papier maché.

settings.title: Drawstring
settings.text: A length of either cotton cord or elastic cord encased within the binding that allows the upper to form a snug fit around the foot.

settings.title: Heel Strap
settings.text: A satin tab which is sewn over the joining seams of the back uppers.

settings.title: Paste
settings.text: A specially formulated glue type substance, which is used in both the process of hardening the toe Block/Box and attaching the insole to the inside of the pointe shoe.

settings.title: Platform
settings.text: The flattened surface at the toe end of the pointe shoe which allows the dancer to balance ‘en pointe’.

settings.title: Pleats
settings.text: The measured pleating which draws the satin over the Box which meets the Outsole.

settings.title: Shank / Insole
settings.text: A combination of layers of special materials into a unique profile which forms the structural anchor similar to the way a spine supports the human body. Shanks/insoles are developed in different profiles creating various levels of flexibility.

settings.title: Side Seam
settings.text: The stitching on the side seam is a double French stitch which ensures strength and sews front Upper to the back Upper.

settings.title: Sock
settings.text: A thin suede or cotton fabric covering the inner shank.

settings.title: Upper
settings.text: All the parts above the shoe’s sole that are joined together to become a single unit which is then attached to the Outsole.

settings.title: Vamp
settings.text: The lower forward part of the shoe’s upper, covering the forepart of the foot and includes the Block/Box and Platform.

settings.title: Vamp (Modified)
settings.text: The measurement from the centre middle of the drawstring to the edge of the Platform.

settings.title: Vamp Shape / Throat Line
settings.text: The shape of the entrance area for the front of the foot. In Bloch pointe shoes the Vamp shape is either ‘U’ shaped or ‘V’ shaped.

settings.title: Wing
settings.text: Each of the two symmetrical sides of the vamp directed toward the heel. The outer edge of the hardened toe Block/Box  that contain  a lesser amount of material and paste. The Wings can vary in shape and hardness depending on the style of pointe shoe or the dancers preference.

settings.title: Foot Shapes
settings.text: Note the overall shape of toe tips as well as the width at point A and point B. Both Greek and Egyptian shapes have a narrow tip and wide tip types.

settings.title: Pointe Shoe Width
settings.text:
Bloch pointe shoes are available in up to four different widths.

Bloch pointe shoe widths can be identified in three different ways depending on the style. Some of the earlier developed styles denote widths with the A, B, C, D, E format and the later styles with either X or Y formats. With the different styles, widths and sizes available, Bloch offers over 1000 variations of pointe shoes.
